title: Building future pathways in Gove
summary: A national careers partnership shaped by local people and language is creating opportunities for Gove’s community.
body_markdown:
That became clear during a TCD session at Dhupuma Barker.


Students were working through a module developed with Yutjuwala Djiwarr Aged Care Centre and translated into local dialect, when they began recognising the people and places appearing on screen.


They spotted people they knew in the videos and eagerly pointed them out to classmates. There was a genuine buzz in the room.


The school already visits the centre each week to read and spend time with Elders, so the module helped students see a familiar place in a new way – as somewhere they could one day work and build a career.


The program is also reaching beyond the school gate.


TCD has been preparing training with the Marngarr Resource Centre, a Yolŋu organisation that delivers training, employment and youth programs, and introducing the modules to young adults and people participating in pathways into work.


With the Gove region continuing to evolve, these partnerships are creating vital opportunities for young people to explore, plan and prepare for the future.


"As the region prepares for life beyond mining, it’s important that local people can see and consider the opportunities that may emerge,” Lauren, our Communities and Social Performance Manager, said.


“This wonderful partnership is helping highlight exciting pathways that are shaped by community and focused on the region's future.”
